summary: The note describes the UEFA Euro 2008 Final, played on 29 June 2008 at the Ernst-Happel-Stadion in Vienna, Austria, to decide the tournament winner. Spain beat Germany 1–0 thanks to a 33rd-minute goal by Fernando Torres. The note also places Spain's record in tournament history, noting they were only the second team to win every group-stage match and the first since Germany in 1996 to win the tournament undefeated.
one_line: Spain beat Germany 1–0 in the Euro 2008 final in Vienna, with Fernando Torres scoring in the 33rd minute.
key_facts: The UEFA Euro 2008 Final was a football match played on 29 June 2008.
The match took place at the Ernst-Happel-Stadion in Vienna, Austria.
The match determined the winner of UEFA Euro 2008.
Spain defeated Germany 1–0 in the UEFA Euro 2008 Final.
Fernando Torres scored the only goal of the UEFA Euro 2008 Final in the 33rd minute.
Spain's group-stage record of winning every match was only the second time this had happened in European Championship history.
France was the other team to win every group-stage match in European Championship history, in 1984.
Spain were the first team since Germany in 1996 to win the tournament undefeated.
The note describes Spain's performance in the final as fairly dominant despite the one-goal margin.
